study.title: Breadth-first search: state-space BFS section only
study.locator: When the pattern bends: State-space BFS (LC 127, LC 752)
study.depth: Read only that section here. The queue mechanics belong to the BFS unit.

focus: Default to the adjacency list on sparse graphs: at n = 10^5 the chapter's arithmetic gives about 1.6 MB for the list against about 10^10 matrix cells. Take the matrix only under n <= 500 with heavy edge tests, and keep the raw edge list for Kruskal and Bellman-Ford.
An undirected edge is two adjacency entries; a directed edge is one. The directed flag belongs in the constructor, not in the traversal.
An implicit graph is a neighbor function, not a table: four lines of grid arithmetic or one-letter word mutations replace a 10,000-vertex grid build.
When the state carries more than the vertex (a word, a lock combination, keys held), the visited mark must sit on the state. Marking the bare vertex merges distinct states.
units.reproduce: From a blank file with the course Python (3.13.14), build the undirected adjacency list for n = 5 and edges [(0,1),(0,2),(1,3),(2,3),(3,4)], assert adj[3] == [1,2,4], then BFS from 0 and report distances {0:0, 1:1, 2:1, 3:2, 4:3}. Then write grid_neighbors(r, c, rows, cols) yielding the four in-bounds neighbors, and state in one sentence why Word Ladder nodes are words rather than positions.
traps: Forgetting the second push for undirected edges: BFS reaches one side of an edge but not the other, and reports disconnected on a connected input.
Building an adjacency list for an edge-centric algorithm: Kruskal sorts the input edge list and Bellman-Ford scans it; neither queries neighbors of one vertex, so the build is pure overhead.
Marking the vertex instead of the state: two paths reaching the same cell with different keys collapse into one visited bit, and the second path is wrongly pruned.

selfTest.q: List, matrix or edge list for BFS on a sparse graph with n = 10^5, and why?
selfTest.a: Adjacency list. Traversal costs Theta(V + E) on the list against Theta(V^2) on the matrix, and the matrix needs about 10^10 cells at that scale.

selfTest.q: LC 1557 answers with an in-degree array and no adjacency list. What is the general lesson?
selfTest.a: Store the minimum structure the algorithm consumes. In-degree-zero detection needs counts, not neighbors.

selfTest.q: Two searches reach grid cell (2,2), one holding key A and one holding nothing. One visited bit on (2,2): what breaks?
selfTest.a: The second arrival is skipped although its future differs: the doors it can open are not the same. The visited key must be (cell, keys).

selfTest.q: Why do Kruskal and Bellman-Ford take the edge list as is?
selfTest.a: They consume edges in bulk order (by weight, or all of them per pass) and never query the neighbors of one vertex.

study.title: Unweighted shortest paths by BFS
study.locator: Chapter 8, Section 8.4 Unweighted Graphs: Breadth-First Search with the FIFO queue and layer analysis (printed pp. 278-281)

focus: Mark visited at enqueue, on the same line as the push. Marking at dequeue lets two queued neighbors push the same vertex again, which turns Theta(V + E) into Theta(V times E) on dense graphs.
The FIFO invariant: the queue always holds vertices at most two consecutive distances from the sources. Draining a full layer before the next is what makes first discovery shortest.
Multi-source BFS seeds every source at depth 0 in one pre-scan, equivalent to a virtual super-source with zero-weight edges. One run replaces one BFS per source.
Counting is an outer scan wrapped around the traversal: every unvisited land cell starts one flood. Minutes count edges traversed; binary-matrix path length counts cells, so it adds one.
units.reproduce: From a blank file with the course Python (3.13.14), run multi-source BFS on [[2,1,1],[1,1,0],[0,1,1]] and return 4; on [[2,1,1],[0,1,1],[1,0,1]] return -1; on a grid with no fresh cells return 0. State the input size (3 by 3) and that the answer counts edges, not cells.
traps: list.pop(0) as a queue: each pop shifts the remaining elements, so at 20,000 queued cells one pop costs about 1.9 us against about 11 ns for deque.popleft (measured on 12th Gen i9-12900K, Python 3.13.14). Always import deque.
A single-source loop over sources for a multi-source question: n runs give n single-source distances, not the parallel-frontier minimum the problem asks for.
Cell-versus-edge counting: LC 994 returns the depth of the last rotted cell while LC 1091 returns depth plus one for the cell-inclusive path. Trace a 3-cell line by hand before submitting.

selfTest.q: Prove BFS first discovery is shortest.
selfTest.a: Induction on layers: sources are distance 0, and the queue dequeues every distance-d vertex before any distance-(d+1) vertex is discovered, since discovery appends to the back. So the first edge reaching v comes from a distance-(dist(v)-1) vertex along a shortest path, and no shorter path can exist or v would have been discovered earlier.

selfTest.q: Why does the super-source argument preserve the bound?
selfTest.a: The virtual source adds one vertex and one zero-weight edge per real source, scanned once in the seed pass. Total work stays Theta(V + E).

selfTest.q: A triangle A->B->C->A with visited marked at dequeue: what happens?
selfTest.a: A enqueues B; B enqueues C before A is popped; C sees A still unmarked-at-pop and enqueues A again. The queue grows without bound on larger cycles; the visited bit at enqueue stops the second push.

selfTest.q: LC 547 reads an n-by-n matrix but runs the same template as LC 200. What changes?
selfTest.a: Only the neighbor function: neighbors of i are columns j with isConnected[i][j] == 1. Cost becomes Theta(n^2) because every matrix cell is read.

study.title: Depth-first search through cycle detection
study.locator: Sections 6.1 to 6.3: Preorder and Postorder, Classifying Vertices and Edges, Detecting Cycles (printed pp. 227-232)

focus: Mark before recursing, on entry. Recursing first lets the neighbor immediately recurse back, which loops until RecursionError.
GRAY means on the current stack; BLACK means finished. The diamond edge into a BLACK vertex is a benign forward edge; only a GRAY neighbor is a back edge and a cycle witness.
Undirected DFS needs one boolean plus the parent argument: the neighbor you arrived from does not count. Three colors are unnecessary there because undirected DFS has no forward or cross edges.
Bipartite colors are 1 and -1 with 0 for unvisited, flipped by negation across each edge, inside an outer loop over components. A same-color edge is the odd-cycle witness.
units.reproduce: From a blank file with the course Python (3.13.14), run three-color DFS on the diamond [(0,1),(0,2),(1,3),(2,3)] and report no cycle, and on [(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)] report a cycle. Then run two-color BFS on [[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2]] (True) and on [[1,2],[0,2],[0,1]] (False).
traps: Two-color directed DFS: the diamond reports a cycle because one visited bit conflates on-stack with finished. The fix is the third color, not a second visited set.
Parentless undirected DFS: a single edge reports a cycle because each endpoint sees the other as visited. The fix is the parent argument, not more colors.

Recursive DFS on deep grids or chains: CPython caps the stack at 1000 frames by default (check with sys.getrecursionlimit), so a snake region or a 2000-chain crashes. Set the limit explicitly or ship the iterative form.

selfTest.q: Prove a directed graph is acyclic iff DFS finds no back edge.
selfTest.a: If a back edge (u,v) exists, v is an ancestor of u, so the tree path from v to u plus the edge closes a cycle. Conversely, in an acyclic graph no edge lands on a GRAY vertex: tree and forward edges go to descendants, cross edges to finished subtrees. The white-path argument in CLRS 20.3 makes this exact.

selfTest.q: Prove a graph is bipartite iff it has no odd cycle.
selfTest.a: If 2-colored, any cycle alternates colors and must return to its start color after an even number of steps, so all cycles are even. If no odd cycle exists, BFS two-coloring never assigns the same color to both ends of an edge: a conflict would close an odd cycle through the BFS tree, contradiction.

selfTest.q: Why does the bipartite outer loop cost nothing on connected graphs?
selfTest.a: Every later start is already colored, so each trips the continue immediately: O(V) checks total. Skipping the loop misses odd cycles hiding in unvisited components.

selfTest.q: LC 130 floods from the border instead of testing each region. Why is the inversion sound?
selfTest.a: Border-connected regions are exactly the ones to keep; DFS marks all of them, so every unmarked O is surrounded by construction. Testing from inside cannot see the border without the same outward walk.
